title: First-match prices need not be pairwise once three rules can match an item
statement: k rules, m items; rule r matches item i or not; if r is the first rule of the order π that matches i, item i pays cost[i][r] (an item matched by no rule pays a fixed default); price(π) is the sum over the items (the price function of the pair entry first-match-rule-ordering-enumeration-vs-subset-dp; costs real here). The price has the pairwise form if price(π) = C + Σ_{x≠y} w_xy [x before y in π] for all orders π. (1) If every item is matched by at most two rules, the price has the pairwise form. (2) For k = 3 rules a, b, c and one item matched by all three with costs (1, 0, 0), price(π) = [a first] does not have the pairwise form; over the 6 orders the least-squares distance to the pairwise functions is exactly 1/3 (minimum sum of squared residuals), attained by −1/6 + ([a before b] + [a before c])/2. More generally, costs (x, y, z) on one item matched by a, b, c give a pairwise price iff x = y = z, and for every k ≥ 3 some instance is not pairwise.

provenance.pending_note: Probably our own result. The sources read on ordering a first-match rule list (Yee, Dahan, Hauser and Orlin 2007; Schmitt and Martignon 2006; Chakravarthy et al. 2008) contain special cases of the problem (0/1 and 0/w costs) and its subset dynamic program, but none of them states the results of this note, which proves them in full. Martignon and Hoffrage (2002), which might contain them, could not be read (no open-access copy found), so whether it does could not be checked.
